question: Which of the 7 outstanding dependency upgrades are safe to take?

gates.protocol: dist/ and *.tsbuildinfo deleted before every build so each run is a real cold build

baseline.audit: pnpm audit --audit-level moderate: No known vulnerabilities found

groups.name: patches: smol-toml, vitest, tsx
notes: All three were ALREADY inside the declared caret ranges (smol-toml ^1.3.0, vitest ^4.1.9, tsx ^4.19.0).
This is therefore a LOCKFILE-ONLY upgrade: no package.json edit is strictly required.
`pnpm update -r` nevertheless raised the range floors and reformatted `engines` in 3 manifests; the cosmetic `engines` churn was reverted for the proposed patch.
vitest 4.1.10 pulled a second vite instance keyed on the new tsx; no behavioural effect observed.

groups.name: @biomejs/biome 2.2.0 -> 2.5.6

detail.manualEquivalenceCheck: Equivalent for this call site: when `inert` is undefined, `inert?.(x)` evaluates to undefined and `!undefined === true`, matching the `!inert` branch; when `inert` exists, both forms test `!inert(x)`. 366/366 tests still pass with the fix applied.

detail.correctRemediation: biome-ignore comment - the literal __proto__ key IS the assertion of this test ('preserves a setup file literally named __proto__'). Applying biome's rewrite would destroy the test's purpose.

detail.rule: config deprecation (info, does not fail the gate)
detail.detail: The configuration schema version does not match the CLI version 2.5.6 ($schema still points at 2.2.0)

detail.rule: config deprecation (info, does not fail the gate)
detail.detail: linter.rules.recommended is deprecated and will be removed in the next Biome major; use `preset` instead

remediationMeasured.effortEstimate: ~15 minutes. Two 1-line source edits plus one config migrate. `biome migrate --write` additionally reformats biome.json to tabs and expands the includes array - hand-edit the 2 config lines instead to keep the diff to 2 lines.

groups.recommendation: DO_NOT_IMPLEMENT as a bare version bump; IMPLEMENT only bundled with the 3 measured remediation edits. The exact pin in package.json is load-bearing - a floating range would let a future minor introduce new rules and break CI on an unrelated PR.

nativeRebuild.typesPackage: @types/better-sqlite3 stayed at 7.6.13; typecheck still passes, so no types bump is needed

crossProcessWalContention.test: packages/coach/src/store.test.ts:815 "recomputeRatings is safe under cross-process contention (L11)"
crossProcessWalContention.shape: 4 real spawned node processes x 25 outcomes x 6 recompute iterations against ONE file-backed WAL db, via packages/coach/test/fixtures/recompute-worker.mjs which imports the BUILT dist/index.js

groups.name: @types/node 22.20.0 -> 26.1.2

whyNotSafeDespitePassingGates.claim: @types/node 26 types APIs that do not exist on the supported Node floor, so tsc stops being a guard against shipping code that crashes for users on Node 22.13.

empiricalDemonstration.api: globalThis.URLPattern (became a Node global in v24)
empiricalDemonstration.underTypes22: tsc error TS2304: Cannot find name 'URLPattern' - the current setup CATCHES it
empiricalDemonstration.conclusion: types 26 turns a compile-time error into a runtime crash for anyone on the declared floor. This is a real regression in safety that no gate in this repo can detect.

whyNotSafeDespitePassingGates.runtimeProbeOfOtherCandidates: Of 12 probed APIs, only URLPattern and Float16Array are absent on Node 22.22.2 (Float16Array is a lib/ES feature, not @types/node). The absent surface is small TODAY but grows with every Node release while the floor stays at 22.13.

groups.recommendation: DO_NOT_IMPLEMENT. Keep @types/node on the 22.x line so the type layer keeps matching engines.node. Revisit only when the engines floor itself moves; the standard rule is to pin @types/node to the OLDEST supported Node major.

groups.name: typescript 6.0.3 -> 7.0.2
groups.verdict: SAFE (contradicts the charter's expectation of maximal breakage)
groups.errorClasses: NONE. Zero compiler errors of any class across all 7 projects and the test typecheck project.
skepticalVerification: Build is not a no-op: 45 .js + 50 .d.ts + 50 .js.map emitted across 7 projects (150 files total).

EMIT EQUIVALENCE: 50/50 .js byte-identical to TS6, 50/50 .d.ts byte-identical to TS6. Only 16/50 .js.map differ, and the difference is confined to the `mappings` string (version/file/sources/sourceRoot/names all identical).

CHECKER IS NOT PERMISSIVE: a 6-case strictness probe (strictNullChecks, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, type mismatch, noImplicitOverride, verbatimModuleSyntax type-only-import-as-value, excess property check) produced IDENTICAL diagnostics under TS7 and TS6 - same error codes, same line:col.
Built CLI runs: `node packages/cli/dist/bin.js --help` prints the full command list.
groups.performance: cold build 7s -> 2s; typecheck 6s -> 3s (TS7 is the native port)
groups.recommendation: NEEDS_OWNER_DECISION. Every gate passes and emit is byte-identical, so this is technically SAFE, but TS7 is a whole-compiler rewrite and a 4-gate suite on a 366-test repo is thin evidence for adopting one. See caveats: editor/IDE tooling, biome's and vitest's TS assumptions, and any tsc API consumers were not exercised.

incidentalObservation.severity: PRE-EXISTING, independent of every E5 upgrade (reproduces on the unmodified baseline)
incidentalObservation.finding: INERT_CLIENT_KEYS is a plain object literal, so `INERT_CLIENT_KEYS[key]` for an INHERITED key resolves to an Object.prototype method instead of undefined, and the key is treated as an allowlisted inert annotation.

probes.extra key toString: normalizeSpawnEntry CLAIMS IT AS OURS and sameEntry() returns true -> foreign entry becomes eligible for deletion on eject
probes.extra key constructor: same: CLAIMED AS OURS, sameEntry() true
probes.extra key valueOf: throws unhandled TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object

measuredAgainstRealBuiltCode.invariantViolated: The function's own docstring says 'ANY other extra key ... makes this null, so a user's lookalike is never mistaken for ours and deleted.'

incidentalObservation.mirrorParity: A scratchpad mirror of the production function matched the REAL built function on 16/16 inputs (12 controls + 4 inherited-key cases), including reproducing both TypeError throws — so the mirror is a faithful stand-in and the proposed fix was evaluated against real behaviour.
incidentalObservation.proposedFixValidation: Object.hasOwn guard: changes 0 of 12 control behaviours, returns null for all 4 inherited-key inputs.
incidentalObservation.notMeasured: No end-to-end eject scenario was driven to actually delete a victim entry; the claim is about normalizeSpawnEntry/sameEntry return values, which are the inputs to that decision. No regression test was written. Reachability depends on whether a real client config can carry such a key, which was not investigated.
incidentalObservation.relationToUpgrade: Independent of the biome bump. Biome's optional-chain rewrite neither introduces nor fixes it (inert is a truthy inherited function either way). Should be triaged separately, NOT folded into the dependency PR.
